title: Model occupancy spline tuning for long-window variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce model-specific occupancy curves (spline-based profiles) and runtime knobs to reduce peak GPU memory for Llama/Mistral/Qwen long-context variants while preserving tail latency and output quality.

Background: We observed sustained high peak allocation for long-window jobs primarily caused by over-reserving KV slices and static eviction thresholds. Continuous batching amplifies transient working-set spikes. Existing memory heuristics are generic and leave 8-20% headroom that could be reclaimed for larger batch concurrency or longer pinned contexts.

Hypothesis: Replacing coarse histogram-based occupancy profiles with per-variant spline-fit occupancy curves combined with adaptive slice sizing and a soft-eviction window will reduce median peak by ~10-15% and 95th percentile by ~8% for 64k/128k seq workloads under continuous batching.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime exposes per-model occupancy spline and a slice_size_schedule tensor config.
- Benchmarks (see artifacts) show >=8% reduction in 95p GPU memory without increasing 95p latency by more than 5% on our reference 8xA100 long-context fleet.
- No regression in generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE-like eval + model-equivalent unit tests).

Experiment matrix (canonical):
- Models: llama-3-32k, mistral-large-64k, qwen-36k (quantized and fp32 variants)
- Configs: baseline (static slices, LRU eviction), spline-occupancy + soft-evict, spline + adaptive-batch-priority, spline + quant-aware slice shrink.
- Workloads: chat-append heavy prefix (avg seq 48k), long-doc streaming (avg seq 80k), mixed short/long duty cycles.

Runtime knobs to land:
- occupancy_spline: base knot points serialized as CSV (knot_x,knot_y) per variant
- slice_schedule_multiplier: float per stage (0.5-1.25) to shrink/grow slices over steps
- soft_evict_window_ms: millisecond window where eviction becomes probabilistic rather than hard
- batch_priority_boost: int weight applied to slices with active streams
- quant_aware_shrink: boolean to shrink slices more aggressively for int8 models

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Occupancy+Splines+for+Long+Context (design v0.3)
- Benchmark dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/bench/longctx-memory-occupancy (compare runs)
- Experimental data: gs://redwood-inference-experiments/occupancy-spline/2025-01 (CSV + flamegraphs)
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 (core allocator changes)
- Example config set: https://github.com/redwood-inference/configs/blob/main/occupancy/spline-sets.yaml

Trade-offs considered:
- More aggressive shrinking can increase eviction churn and latency; mitigated with soft_evict_window and batch_priority_boost.
- Per-variant splines add config surface area; plan to auto-generate defaults from profiling runs and expose only a small set of tuning knobs in Console.

Next steps:
1) Finish spline fitting tooling to convert recent profiling traces into knot sets (owner: Luca).
2) Land allocator feature flags and a minimal runtime toggle for canary (owner: infra team).
3) Run fleet canary on dedicated pool (canary subset) and collect 7d of telemetry.
4) Prep rollout plan with rollback SLOs and console visibility (owner: PM).

Long-term: Plug occupancy splines into Optimize engine to auto-suggest slice_schedule_multiplier based on target cost/latency trade-off.
